# fable.rjd3 <img src="man/figures/logo.png" align="right" alt="" />

<!-- badges: start -->
[![R universe version](https://aqlt.r-universe.dev/badges/fable.rjd3)](https://aqlt.r-universe.dev/fable.rjd3)
[![R-CMD-check](https://github.com/AQLT/fable.rjd3/actions/workflows/R-CMD-CHECK.yaml/badge.svg)](https://github.com/AQLT/fable.rjd3/actions/workflows/R-CMD-CHECK.yaml)
<!-- badges: end -->

`fable.rjd3` brings the seasonal adjustment algorithms of
[JDemetra+ v3](https://github.com/jdemetra/jdplus-main) to the
[`fable`](https://fable.tidyverts.org/) framework. It lets you seasonally
adjust `tsibble` series with the standard `model()` / `components()` workflow,
on one or many series at once, and gives access to everything JDemetra+
computes.

* **Four models**: `X13()` (X-13ARIMA), `TRAMOSEATS()` (TRAMO-SEATS), and the
  pre-adjustment models `REGARIMA()` and `TRAMO()`.
* **Full control of the specification**, either with the specification objects
  of the `rjd3*` packages or with specials in the model formula, including
  regressors taken from the columns of the `tsibble`.
* **Standard verbs**: `components()`, `forecast()`, `glance()`, `tidy()`,
  `report()`, `fitted()`, `residuals()`, `augment()`, `outliers()`, `refit()`,
  `stream()`, and `backcast()`.
* **Any JDemetra+ indicator** with `jd3_indicator()`, from the Java result kept in the model.
* **JDemetra+ workspaces**: `import_jws()` and `export_jws()`.

## Installation

`fable.rjd3` is built on the JDemetra+ v3 R packages (`rjd3toolkit`, `rjd3x13`, `rjd3tramoseats` and `rjd3workspace`), which requires Java 21 or higher. 

To install the developpment version:

- From [r-universe](https://aqlt.r-universe.dev/fable.rjd3):

```{r, echo = TRUE, eval = FALSE}
install.packages("fable.rjd3", repos = c("https://aqlt.r-universe.dev", "https://cloud.r-project.org"))
```

- From GitHub:

```{r, echo = TRUE, eval = FALSE}
# install.packages("pak")
pak::pak("AQLT/fable.rjd3")
```


## Example

The series must be a regular, univariate `tsibble` with a `yearmonth` or
`yearquarter` index. Monthly, bimonthly, quarterly, four-monthly and semi-annual
series are supported: the frequency is deduced from the interval between
observations (for example, a `yearmonth` index with a step of 6 months is a
semi-annual series).

```{r example-fit}
library(fable.rjd3)

air <- as_tsibble(AirPassengers)

mb <- model(
    air,
    x13 = X13(value),
    ts  = TRAMOSEATS(value)
)
mb
```

`components()` returns the decomposition as a `dable` (trend, seasonal,
irregular and seasonally adjusted series):

```{r example-components}
components(mb)
```

```{r example-plot, eval = requireNamespace("ggtime", quietly = TRUE), fig.height = 6}
library(ggtime)
ggplot2::autoplot(components(mb))
```

### Specification

The specification is set with the `spec` argument, or with specials in the
formula:

```{r example-spec}
mb_log <- model(
    air,
    x13 = X13(
        value ~ transform(fun = "Log") +
            outlier(outliers.type = c("AO", "LS")),
        spec = "rsa3"
    )
)
```

### Diagnostics

```{r example-diag}
glance(mb)
tidy(mb_log)
report(mb["x13"])
```

### Forecasts

The forecasts of the raw series come from the pre-adjustment model, as
distributions:

```{r example-forecast}
forecast(mb, h = 12)
```

### Updating a model

```{r example-update}
air_old <- air[air$index < yearmonth("1960 Jan"), ]
air_new <- air[air$index >= yearmonth("1960 Jan"), ]

mb_old <- model(air_old, x13 = X13(value))
mb_new <- stream(mb_old, air_new)   # refresh policy "Fixed" by default
```

### JDemetra+ workspaces

```{r example-ws, eval = FALSE}
mb <- import_jws("path/to/workspace.xml")   # keys: `sap` and `series`
export_jws(mb, "path/to/new_workspace.xml")
```
